question: Does a separately implemented Rust quadratic-field/point-sum validator reproduce both directions of the recorded S3 prime-field population, locally and on a separately provisioned free GitHub-hosted runner?

claims.text: Actual finite quadratic extensions supply all base-coordinate square lifts and the actual Mathlib pair oracle matches S3, under its stated hypotheses. Decided by Lean.
Full Rust aggregates match the seen known-answer C++ population on each execution host, with every internal inverse/root/point check passing.
Remote execution requires actual workflow/job output. An API/registration rejection is not-completed, not independent validation.
Compiler/runtime proofs, signed execution verification, binary/S4/S5/degree validation and full independence from the producing author are outside scope.

flags.binary_identity: compiled separately per host; measured before native work

stopping_rules.rule: One full local call and one permitted manual remote dispatch. Retain every output/rejection; no outcome-dependent rerun.
Compile timeout60s,native30s,remote job5minutes; no paid or alternate-runner retry.

decision_rule.text: known_answer_pass for each actually completed exact match. Independent-host replication requires actual GitHub-hosted job evidence; rejection or missing execution is not_validated, never inferred from a prepared workflow.
decision_rule.statistic: exact complete per-field integer equality and native inverse/root/point checks
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: integer discrepancies from the fixed reference; no population inference

inadmissible: Calling seen C++reference/preflight a blind discovery.
Claiming independent-host execution before actual job evidence.
Rerouting a rejected dispatch through a trusted verifier or paid/EKS/larger runner.
Changing frozen Rust,driver,comparator,workflow or reference after data without a labelled amendment.
Claiming compiler/runtime proof, signed execution standing or complete binary/S4/S5/degree validation.
